t: Find Subarray With Bitwise OR Closest to K
o: We want a contiguous subarray whose OR is as close as possible to k. OR only gains bits as the subarray grows, so for a fixed right endpoint r the set of achievable OR values of subarrays ending at r is small: each bit can turn on at most once, giving at most ~30 distinct values. In Example 1, subarray [1,2] ORs to 3 = k, difference 0. In Example 3 the only subarray ORs to 1, difference 9.
k: For a fixed right endpoint, extending leftward monotonically adds bits, so there are at most log(max) ≈ 30 distinct OR values ending at each index.
Maintain the list of distinct ORs of subarrays ending at the current index: new list = {x} ∪ {prev | x}, deduplicated.
Answer = min over all maintained values of |k − v|.

a.n: Approach 1: Distinct ORs Ending at Each Index
a.i: Sweep left to right carrying the set S of OR values of all subarrays ending at the previous index. When the new element x arrives, every subarray ending here is either [x] alone or a previous subarray extended by x, so the new set is {x} ∪ {v | x for v in S}. Deduplication caps the set at ~30 entries, making the whole sweep near-linear.
s: Initialize an empty list cur and answer = infinity.
For each x: build cur = dedupe([x] + [v|x for v in cur]).
Update answer with min |k − v| over cur.
a.t: O(n log C) — each step processes at most ~30 distinct OR values (log C bits)
a.sp: O(log C) — the deduplicated OR-value list

a.i: Equivalently, track for each bit the latest index where it was set. The OR of the best subarray ending at r can be reconstructed from those bits; combined with a sorted structure this yields the same complexity, but the sliding-set method above is simpler and equally fast, so it is preferred in practice.
s: Keep last[b] = most recent index setting bit b.
At each r, OR together bits whose last occurrence ≥ some l to enumerate candidate ORs.
a.t: O(n log² C) — for each index, ~30 candidate left endpoints each rebuilt over 31 bits

w: Use Approach 1 in an interview — it is shorter and faster. Key pitfall: forgetting to deduplicate lets the list grow to O(n). Note the answer can never be improved past 0, so early-exit when |k−v| = 0 is a nice micro-optimization. Follow-ups may ask to report the actual subarray — keep (value, left endpoint) pairs in the sliding set.
